messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated cross-region routing error rate for requests from APAC -> EU (region steering imbalance). Detect window: 2m, error spike 18%. Auto-detect triggered.

sylvie (oncall): paging in. I'm on it. seeing increased 5xxs and latency for eu models from ap-southeast.

joan (sre): I see the same in traces — higher p50/p95 on eu nodes for APAC-origin requests. Seems like some requests are being routed to outdated pinned variants.

raj (neteng): looking at routing-control-plane logs. We had a policy rollout 08:12 UTC that updated latency-steering buckets; some regions got the new policy but eu-west retained old pin entries. Could be a policy-eval race.

maria (prod-ops): any customer-facing impact yet? support pinging top customers.

eli (support): two customers reported degraded inference latency and increased timeouts in the last 5m: acme-inc and fin-app. Creating incident RCA ticket.

sylvie (oncall): ok immediate plan: 1) disable latency-steering rollout to stop further policy changes 2) pin traffic to eu-west stable pool 3) mitigate customer impact 4) escalate to neteng if policy store mismatch continues.

raj (neteng): agreed. disabling rollout now. Command: ```curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/policies/rollout/disable -d '{"rollout_id":"rl-2026-08-12-01"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"```

deploy-bot: Rollout rl-2026-08-12-01: disable request accepted by sylvie at 2005554327. Status: stopping further evaluations.

joan (sre): while that stops new changes, the problem looks like evaluation race applying inconsistent pin state between regions. For mitigation we can apply a temporary manual override: set routing policy "pin_override":"eu-west:force" for APAC origins.

maria (prod-ops): how do we apply pin override safely?

raj (neteng): apply via console or API. Example: ```PATCH /policies/region-steering/12345 { "overrides": [{"from_region":"apac","to_region":"eu-west","mode":"force"}], "ttl": 600 }``` I'll push a short-lived TTL 10m and monitor.

sylvie (oncall): raj, go ahead. joan, monitor p95 and error-rate for next 3 minutes. eli, send customer notes: "We’re aware of increased latency, applying routing override to stabilize connections; minimalized impact expected."

raj (neteng): override applied at 2005554342. TTL 600s. Verifying propagation to edge controllers.

joan (sre): metrics updating — error rate falling from 18% -> 4% over 90s. p95 latency trending down. Looks like override helped.

eli (support): Sent notifications to affected customers and posted a brief status to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating latency for APAC->EU requests; mitigations in progress."

maria (prod-ops): do we need an on-call handoff? sylvie, any ETA for stable fix?

sylvie (oncall): I'll keep the incident and follow the rollback plan. If override holds, we should revert the rollout and re-deploy policy with deterministic evaluation ordering. ETA 45m for full verification and safe rollout. If anyone needs to take over at 2005554400 please @sylvie.

joan (sre): root cause hypothesis: rollout evaluation race where policy shards applied at different times produced transient conflicting pin maps; edge controllers fallback logic didn't reconcile quickly, causing a subset of requests to hit stale variants. Postmortem actions: add strong ordering / version check during policy activation, add watch to detect per-region divergence, and add automatic local reconcilers.

raj (neteng): collecting control-plane logs and candidate repro. Will also surface a change to rollout orchestration to require quorum ack before switching traffic.

sylvie (oncall): good. For now we keep override in place until rollout is fully reversed. Monitor windows: next check 2005554370. If stable, we will schedule controlled re-rollout tomorrow.

joan (sre): check at 2005554370: metrics stable, error-rate 2.1%, p95 within SLO. Proceed to stand down alerts to non-critical channels.

eli (support): customers updated. No new incidents reported.

maria (prod-ops): summary for incident log: timeframe 2005554321-2005554380, initial trigger: latency-steering rollout; mitigation: disabled rollout + temporary APAC->EU force pin override TTL 10m; customer impact: degraded latency/timeouts for APAC origins affecting two named customers; resolution: override reduced errors to baseline; follow-ups: rollout orchestration fixes, versioned activation, monitoring for per-region divergence.

sylvie (oncall): handing off to joan for post-incident tasks at 2005554380. I'll remain reachable if needed. :white_check_mark:
